headword: {書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}

definitions.explanation: A postal service in which the item is tracked and recorded at each stage of delivery, providing proof that it was sent and received. Offers compensation if the item is lost or damaged.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧な⟦{書類|しょるい}→書類：01103_shorui⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{送|おく}ろう→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: Let's send the important documents by registered mail.

examples.japanese: {書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{窓口|まどぐち}→窓口：03154_madoguchi⟧でしか⟦{差|さ}し{出|だ}せない→差し出す：04234_sashidasu⟧。
examples.english: Registered mail can only be posted at the counter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{合格|ごうかく}→合格：02816_goukaku⟧⟦{通知|つうち}→通知：04061_tsuuchi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{受|う}け{取|と}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦サイン→サイン：03846_sain⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The acceptance notice arrived by registered mail, so I signed for it.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{書留|かきとめ}→書留：00150_kakitome⟧ (registered, recorded) and ⟦{郵便|ゆうびん}→郵便：03803_yuubin⟧ (mail). Often shortened to just ⟦{書留|かきとめ}→書留：00150_kakitome⟧ in everyday conversation.

TYPES:
- {一般書留|いっぱんかきとめ} — general registered mail (full tracking, higher compensation)
- {簡易書留|かんいかきとめ} — simplified registered mail (basic tracking, lower cost and compensation)
- {現金書留|げんきんかきとめ} — cash registered mail (for sending money in a special envelope)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{送|おく}る→送る：00742_okuru⟧ — to send by registered mail
- {書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧ — to receive registered mail
- {書留郵便|かきとめゆうびん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{追跡|ついせき}→追跡：09722_tsuiseki⟧ — tracking of registered mail

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{普通郵便|ふつうゆうびん}→普通郵便：25818_futsuuyuubin⟧ — regular mail (no tracking or compensation)
- ⟦{速達|そくたつ}→速達：04393_sokutatsu⟧ — express delivery
- ⟦{配達証明|はいたつしょうめい}→配達証明：25813_haitatsushoumei⟧ — delivery certification (an add-on service proving delivery)
- {内容証明|ないようしょうめい} — certified content mail (certifies the content of the letter)

PRACTICAL NOTE:
Registered mail in Japan requires the sender to go to a post office counter; it cannot be dropped in a mailbox. The recipient must sign or stamp (⟦{印鑑|いんかん}→印鑑：05290_inkan⟧ or signature) upon delivery. It is commonly used for sending important documents, certificates, and valuables.
